AGENDA ITEMS AND ACTIONS
5:00 P.M. CLOSED SESSION

CALL TO ORDER Mayor Lainez called the closed session meeting to order at 5:09 pm.

ROLL CALL City Clerk Sarmiento took roll call: All five members of the city council were present.

PUBLIC COMMENT ON CLOSED SESSION ITEMS

RECESS TO CLOSED SESSION  -  Action: approve Mayor Lainez directed City Clerk Sarmiento to read the items listed on the closed session agenda. City Clerk Sarmiento read aloud the two items listed on the closed session agenda.

Mayor Lainez recessed to closed session at 5:10 pm

RECONVENE TO OPEN SESSION Mayor Lainez Reconvened the closed session meeting at 6:16  pm. He then requested city attorney Noel Tapia provide his report from closed session. 

ORAL CLOSED SESSION ANNOUNCEMENT City Attorney Noel Tapia provided a report from closed session.

He stated that with all five members of the city council present the two items listed on the closed session were discussed. Regarding Item number one (1) under anticipated litigation on two (2) cases, staff provided a presentation, city council provided direction and no reportable action was taken. Regarding item two (2) listed as existing litigation, staff provided the city council a presentation, council provided direction and no reportable action was taken. That concluded the city attorneys report.

6:00 P.M. - CITY COUNCIL MEETING

CALL TO ORDER Mayor Lainez called the concurrent joint meetings of the City Council to order at 6:18 pm.

ROLL CALL City Clerk Sarmiento took roll call.

PLEDGE OF ALLEGIANCE The Pledge of Allegiance was led by Director of Finance Alvaro Castellon.

INVOCATION Council Member Rebollo offered the invocation.

APPEARANCES AND PRESENTATIONS None

PUBLIC COMMENT

                                         . CONSENT CALENDAR  -  Action: approve (Pass) Moved by Oralia Rebollo Council Member Rebollo motioned to approved items one (1) through six (6), eight (8) and nine (9) of the consent calendar, seconded by council member Argumedo. Motion carried by unanimous consent.

SCHEDULED MATTERS

10.. PRESENTATION/UPDATE FROM THE SHERIFF'S DEPARTMENT OF PUBLIC SAFETY IN THE CITY OF COMMERCE A report and presentation was provided by Sergeant Cortez on public safety and numbers related to police efforts.

CITY COUNCIL/SUCCESSOR AGENCY REPORTS Council Member Rebollo thanked staff and the community for attending the National Night Out event, and shared her gratitude with staff and there cohesiveness in there execution of the National Night Out event. She then recommended that more food be kept on stand by for attendee's in the future. She suggested a registration be implemented for residents next years event. Residents would be able to register using there residents cards to confirm attendance which will allow for better preparation in regard to the amount of food need for the event. She stressed the importance of having enough food for the residents in attendance of the event. She then thanked the community for their participation in the cultural excursion. She closed by giving her condolences to the family of Tina Gonzalez for there loss.

Council Member Argumedo congratulated staff on a successful National Night Out event and agreed with his counterpart council member Rebollo regarding the need for improvements regarding the food. He also thanked the community for their participation in the cultural excursion event. He concluded he comments by suggesting staff look into a new bus vendor for future cultural excursion events.

Council Member Altamirano also mentioned the successful National Night Out event and thanked staff for their effort. He also shared the positive feedback he received regarding the cultural excursion event. He also agreed with his colleagues on the suggestion to look into a new bus rental vendor for future events.

Mayor Pro Tem Garcia thanked staff and the Police Department team for their participation in a successful National Night Out event. She also mentioned the positive feedback she received regarding the cultural excursion event. She closed her comments by giving her condolences to the Gonzalez family for their loss.

Mayor Lainez spoke on the success of the National Night Out event and the numerous resource and partners that were in attendance at the event. He thanked staff and sponsors for all their hard work to make the event a success. He also mentioned the success of the cultural excursion event and the positive feedback he received from participants. He then encouraged the community to attend the upcoming community events which included the back to school bash. He closed by also sharing his condolences to the family of Valentina Gonzalez for their loss.

ADJOURNMENT Mayor Lainez adjourned the city council meeting in memory of Valentina Gonzalez at 7:27 pm.

Written materials distributed to the City Council are available for public inspection immediately following the posting of this agenda (at least 72 hours prior to a regular City Council meetings) in the City Clerk's Office, at Commerce City Hall, 2535 Commerce Way, Commerce, California, and the Central Library, 5655 Jillson Street, Commerce, California.

Meeting facilities are accessible to persons with disabilities. ln compliance with the Americans with Disabilities Act (ADA) if you need special assistance to participate in this meeting, notify the Office of the City Clerk at (323) 722-4805 at least 24 hours prior to the meeting.

11.. URGENCY ORDINANCE ESTABLISHING A TEMPORARY (45-DAY) MORATORIUM ON DATA CENTER DEVELOPMENT PURSUANT TO CALIFORNIA GOVERNMENT CODE SECTION 65858

RECOMMENDATION:

It is recommended that the City Council consider:

1.	Adopting the proposed Urgency Ordinance, by a four-fifths (4/5) vote, establishing a temporary 45-day moratorium on the acceptance, processing, and approval of any applications, permits, entitlements, or other approvals for data center development within the City of Commerce, pursuant to California Government Code, Section 65858, effective immediately upon adoption; and

2.	Directing the City Manager to return to the City Council within 35 days with a written report describing the measures taken to alleviate the conditions that led to the adoption of this Urgency Ordinance, and to schedule a duly noticed public hearing to consider extension of the moratorium for an additional period of up to 10 months and 15 days.
  -  Action: approve as amended (Pass) Moved by Kevin Lainez Community Development director Jessica Serrano provided a report on the Urgency Ordinance.
